title: Opening praise and the question of the Spirit
english: A synodal letter of Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium. Even before your letters arrived from your love, report had reached us of the purity of your faith, how it is being stretched toward dangers and is steadfast amid sufferings for Christ, and how firm in you is love for God and hope for the future. And now that we have encountered the letters of your reverence, we have truly seen the character of an apostolic church and the zeal of good shepherds, an unwearying diligence befitting true Christians. For you did not reckon the length of the road, nor did you bring your inquiries separately, but you made your request together through your letters. This has made us very hopeful that, having written with one accord, you will also receive our answers with one accord; and we received the harmony in your letters as a kind of prelude to a more perfect unity of mind.

It was our prayer to welcome to the synod the most admirable bishop Basil, who is named with all reverence, and to have him as a sharer—or rather as the leader—in our dealings with you. But since an overwhelming bodily illness prevented him from coming, it is a mark of your perfect love that you did not overlook even the letters of our smallness. Yet we have not left your holy church without a share in his voice either. Since we have a treatise of his composed specifically on this very subject, through that writing we have him speaking together with us. What, then, is the answer to your inquiry?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, opens a synodal letter to fellow bishops, praising their faith and their joint inquiry, and noting that Basil's treatise on the Spirit is being sent with the letter.
